cases.purpose: The case's own PTY as recipient: write with arguments delivers the banner, the escaped message (ESC -> ^[, 0xE9 -> \351) and EOF; after chmod 600 on the terminal, write refuses with the messages-disabled diagnostic and delivers nothing; in stdin mode, two lines typed on the canonical terminal and ^D are delivered after the banner, followed by EOF.
cases.script:
t=$(tty); chmod 620 "$t" || echo chmod-failed >> rc
export BASHWALL_USER=u BASHWALL_HOST=h
write "$t" hi $'a\033[31mb\351'; echo "args=$?" >> rc
chmod 600 "$t"
BASHWALL_USER=refused write "$t" nope 2> err; echo "disabled=$?" >> rc
[[ $(< err) == *"$t has messages disabled"* ]] && echo diagnosed >> rc
chmod 620 "$t"
printf 'READY-STDIN\n'
BASHWALL_USER=s write "$t"; echo "stdin=$?" >> rc

steps.expect:
Message from s@h on pts/[0-9]+ at [0-2][0-9]:[0-5][0-9] \.\.\.+
line one+
line two+
EOF+

cases.oracle:
wall.c header and write_doc/wall_doc: write TTY [MSG...] banner '
\a\a\aMessage from USER@HOST on SRCTTY at HH:MM ...
', message escaped like util-linux fputs_careful (control -> ^X, DEL -> ^?, bytes >= 0x80 -> \NNN, LF -> CRLF), trailing 'EOF
'; refuses when the target lacks S_IWGRP|S_IWOTH ('has messages disabled'); stdin is read to EOF when no MSG; wall walks $BASHWALL_UTMP USER_PROCESS records with a line (':' lines skipped), each line once, banner '
Broadcast message from USER@HOST (TTY) (DATE):\a\a
', BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1 suppresses it, -n as non-root warns and keeps it, -g GROUP via $BASHWALL_GROUP_FILE members or $BASHWALL_PASSWD_FILE primary gid. util-linux term-utils write.c/wall.c are the cited behaviour sources; the candidate's TTY-path and environment interfaces have no util-linux equivalent, so these are contract cases.
cases.comparison: contract: raw PTY bytes matched by regex (HH:MM and pts number variable; \r+ allows the terminal's ONLCR on the CRLF the builtin writes); rc lines; absence of the refused banner in the whole output

cases.purpose: Write faults: with /dev/full as the target, the banner write fails with ENOSPC (diagnostic, rc 1); with BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1 the message write fails the same way.
cases.script:
write /dev/full hi 2> err1; echo "banner=$?" > rc
[[ $(< err1) == *'write /dev/full: No space left on device'* ]] && echo banner-enospc >> rc
BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1 write /dev/full hi 2> err2; echo "body=$?" >> rc
[[ $(< err2) == *'write /dev/full: No space left on device'* ]] && echo body-enospc >> rc
